summary: Read-only UI audit verification of 14 P1/P2 fixes on live-DB DynoPay preview. Logged in as hostbay, exercised dashboard, transactions, pay-links, developer-keys, customers, notifications, settings, /about, /for/creators, /system-status, public /pay checkout, public /hostbay + /hostbay/shop, mobile /create-pay-link, /auth/login, /auth/register, /wallet, /invoices, /storefront, /fees. 13 of 14 fixes verified PASSING. Only 1 fix regressed/incomplete: Customers row-name mapping still renders raw 'Recovered Customer' string (banner + API chip are present, but displayFor() literal-match is not firing so the friendly label ('API customer (restored)'/'API payments') never appears). No write actions performed.

ui_bugs.issue:
All 24 rows on /customers still display the raw DB literal 'Recovered Customer' + 'API' chip. The displayFor() branch that maps DB kind === 'Recovered Customer' to i18n key customers.recoveredCustomerName ('API customer (restored)') / customers.apiCustomerName ('API payments') is not triggering. Banner [data-testid='customers-api-banner'] IS present and correct, and the API origin chip renders, so only the name-cell mapping is broken. Likely cause: comparison is on customer.name / customer.type but the field carrying 'Recovered Customer' is different (e.g. customer.customer_type or customer.status), or the locale keys weren't added to the running locale bundle. Confirmed via row.innerText: 'Recovered Customer

API
 | 

No customer details provided

 | 

$0.00

 | 

0 txns

 | 

Jul 11, 2026'.

action_items: FIX Customers page: In Components/Page/Customers/index.tsx displayFor(), verify which field carries the 'Recovered Customer' literal from the API — likely the field is customer.customer_type or customer.type rather than customer.name. Currently the mapping compares against the wrong property so all 24 rows fall through to the raw DB literal. Add a case-insensitive fallback and confirm langs/locales/en/common.json ships customers.apiCustomerName='API payments' and customers.recoveredCustomerName='API customer (restored)' keys are wired to the running t() namespace. Repro: log in as hostbay, open /customers — every row shows 'Recovered Customer'.
critical_code_review_comments: The customers displayFor mapping fix (item #7) is the only one that regressed. Recommend adding a Jest/RTL test that asserts a customer object with type='Recovered Customer' renders as 'API customer (restored)' — this would have caught it.
Landing '/' hit networkidle timeout at 30s (non-blocking, other pages fine). Consider deferring heavy hero imagery to below-the-fold or preconnecting to Next image domain.
Playwright could not reliably locate the theme toggle button (no aria-label). Add data-testid='theme-toggle' to the header sun/moon button to make regression tests deterministic.

rca of the issue: Customers row rendering still shows raw 'Recovered Customer'. The fix commit added a displayFor() case for kind==='Recovered Customer', a banner with data-testid='customers-api-banner' (verified present), and locale keys apiCustomerName/recoveredCustomerName. The banner + API chip render correctly, meaning the code path executes and locale bundle loads. Therefore the string-comparison inside displayFor() is against a field that does NOT contain 'Recovered Customer' — most likely displayFor is reading customer.name while the actual DB literal lives on customer.customer_type / customer.type / customer.kind. Mitigation: switch the equality check to a normalized union — e.g. const kind = (c.customer_type||c.type||c.name||'').toLowerCase(); if (kind==='recovered customer' || c.origin==='api') return t('customers.recoveredCustomerName'); Reproduction: log in as hostbay -> /customers -> every one of the 24 rows in the table shows 'Recovered Customer' with the API chip.
